name: bansuri_lead
description: Indian bansuri line: states the hook second, passes the tune on and returns in the lift and the return.
character: A bamboo transverse flute in the singing style of the Hindustani bansuri: notes lean in with a short glide, long notes carry a slow gentle wobble, and the 2.5 to 3.8 kHz band is kept smooth so the lead never pierces.
sources: KB flutes (bansuri bamboo flute: pitch range MIDI 55-86, legato glide about 140 ms, gamaka rate about 6.2 Hz and depth about 45 cents, piercing ratio 2.5-3.8 kHz kept low)
KB indian-film-fusion (the stage-and-dance model of a gamaka; a breathy flute answers at phrase ends)
ESTIMATE: the SoundFont flute stands in for a bansuri; glides are written into the notes, the wobble is not modelled by the sampler
KB flutes (bansuri vibrato: delay 220 ms, rate 5.1 Hz, depth 14 cents)

MEASURED: the mastered file had click events at the onsets of overlapping notes, where the sampler tick lands on a still-ringing note and soften_onsets leaves it alone by design; STARTING VALUE: low-pass at 7000 Hz, above what a phone speaker returns
